Maria G.: heads-up, after rolling microbatch-merge v3 last night we saw a ~2x jump in p95 latency for 1-8 token requests on gpu-pool-7. Notable increase right after 03:12 UTC.

deploy-bot: Deployed microbatch-merge v3 -> canary -> gpu-pool-7 at 2026-03-16T03:10:44Z :white_check_mark:

Alex R.: ugh. Is this the change that merges very small requests into 4-8 token microbatches instead of letting them run solo?

Maria G.: yes. The idea was to increase utilization by merging tiny requests aggressively and then let kernel selection pick fast path. But profiling shows more kernel fallback churn.

Jordan L.: can you paste the perf summaries? p50/p95/p99 and qps?

Maria G.: quick snippet from telemetry (can post full later):
```
route: text-gen-small
baseline (v2): p50=12ms p95=46ms p99=120ms qps=320
v3 (post-rollout): p50=15ms p95=92ms p99=210ms qps=310
error rate unchanged
```

Sam T.: interesting that qps didn't go up much, p95 doubled. That suggests batching isn't improving tail -- maybe KV cache miss amplification or kernel selection cost.

Anya P.: did the microbatch merger change how we tag sequence-length histograms for the kernel selector? iirc we had a guard that forces FP16 fused kernel for seq<=16. If merging increases effective seq length seen by selector, it might flip kernels.

Maria G.: exact suspicion. I pulled a flamegraph from one of the slow requests (attached): shows frequent switch between fused-attn kernel and fallback attention with memcpy overhead when merged batches include a mix of tiny and medium-length contexts.

Alex R.: can you paste the flame output (or profiler command) here?

Maria G.: profiler dump:
```
# sample stack (top down)
runtime_dispatch()
select_optimal_kernel(seq_len=7, batch=5, kv_present=true)
fused_attn_kernel()
fallback_attention()
memcpy_device_to_device()
kv_cache_lookup()
```

Jordan L.: kv_present=true is suspicious. If KV cache hits are per-request but we merged requests with different key shapes, we might be forcing materialization or eviction thrash. Any cache-miss rate changes?

Maria G.: cache hit rate decreased ~6% for that route around the same window. Also eviction count spiked by ~3x for pool-7.

Sam T.: that aligns: merging requests can increase per-batch memory pressure, pushing kernels to fallback and causing KV shuffles. Two levers: 1) change merger to respect KV-affinity (don't merge reqs that have active kv state), 2) enforce kernel-selection guard to prefer fused path for small seqs even if merged batch has variance.

Anya P.: I'd add a third: add a micro-sampling check before final batch commit. If the batch has >30% variance in seq_len or kv flags, split it. Cheap to compute since we already maintain histograms in the queue.

Alex R.: agree. Also we should consider token budget targets: current target 64 tokens/batch might be too aggressive for small-req-heavy routes; reduce to 32 for these routes.

Maria G.: plan proposal: revert canary -> scale down v3 on pool-7 to 10% traffic, add kv-affinity filter + seq-variance split, and lower token budget for text-gen-small. Rolling out as a patch today.

deploy-bot: Starting rollback of microbatch-merge v3 from 100% -> 10% on gpu-pool-7 at 03:37 UTC :wrench:

Jordan L.: also we should capture kernel selection debug logs when we hit p95>80ms — add a lightweight event with stack id and kernel choice. No blocking perf cost.

Maria G.: added a github PR for the filters and token-budget change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821. Patch includes:
- kv_affinity flag on merger
- seq_variance_threshold split (threshold=0.3)
- per-route token_budget override (default 64 -> 32 for text-gen-small)

Sam T.: can we simulate with the offline request trace set before applying? Keen to know if eviction still spikes.

Maria G.: yes replayed trace on staging with patch. Results: p95 drop back to ~50ms, kv-evictions down 80%, qps roughly same. Will run longer soak.

Anya P.: nice. After soak, let's also run kernel-selection A/B where merged batches include a forced fused kernel path to measure absolute kernel overhead difference. Could be helpful if we want to relax variance constraints later.

Alex R.: assign owners: Maria -> rollout and monitor; Jordan -> kernel-selection debug logging; Sam -> eviction metric dashboard and alert; Anya -> run fused-kernel experiment.

Maria G.: noted. I'll keep this thread updated. If we see re-occurrence after the partial rollback, we'll open an incident. Thanks all :pray:

perf-bot: p95 alert cleared for text-gen-small on gpu-pool-7 at 03:58 UTC :white_check_mark:

Maria G.: closing loop: full rollback to v2 on pool-7 complete, metrics back to baseline after 20m. PR merged to add safe-guards and token budget change, will schedule a controlled canary next week with additional logging.

Alex R.: great work catching the kernel flip. Lesson: merging heuristics must be KV-aware and variance-aware.

Jordan L.: filing a short postmortem doc for eng-runtime notes — I'll link here when done.

Maria G.: thanks everyone!
